newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent trades sideways after bouncy start.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent trades sideways after bouncy start.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures were holding steady just below Friday's close with a raft of bullish technical indicators supporting bull sentiment, traders said.

Prices initially dipped to test $20.04 support as expected, but despite overnight easing in NYMEX crude buying in anticipation of further gains later today, the market pulled back from opening lows to trade in a narrow range between 5-10 cents down.
By 1130 GMT the July Brent contract was trading 10 cents down at $20.25 a barrel.
Analysts are now looking for a test of $28.60, riday's high, and then the $20.84 high made back in March.
Traders had expected an early correction to Friday's gains with the upside effects of funds buying on NYMEX crude having petered out, but technical chart formations continue to confirm the uptrend.
"Technical indicators remain mostly bullish for futures on both sides of the Atlantic although relative strength indicators for NYMEX heating oil have turned a little bearish," a broker said.
The June gas oil contract stood $4.50 higher at $177.50 a tonne.
